PRIOR ATTEMPT CHECKED: aliases.py, held_rows.json and held_spec.txt reused after checks. Every held row exists on its shelf with that author. Two picks were wrong and are replaced: Paisius Velichkovsky (the first pick was a letter by the Neamt elders Sofronii and Athanasius, not by him; now his own writings) and Charles Wesley (the first pick was the hymn collection John Wesley edited; now Charles's own Journal, author slug wesley-c, not wesley-charles; the shelf has both slugs for him).

JOINT: Konrad Grebel's quote is a joint letter with Marx Bosshard. Katharine Evans and Sarah Cheevers share one held row, their joint narrative. Mekhitar's letter is 'from himself and his monks'. Ziegenbalg's held row is the Tranquebar missionaries' joint letters.

REPORTED SPEECH (the person's words as someone else set them down): Andrew Melville (James Melville's diary), Margaret Clitherow (John Mush), Simon Episcopius (Calder's version of Limborch), Ann Lee (testimonies gathered decades later), Gustav Vasa (quoted by Anjou). Each is in direct quotation in its source. Mark may judge whether reported speech counts as 'their own words'.

ISSUED IN THEIR NAME: Afonso I's letter was written by his scribe ('dom Joham teyxeira o fez'). Christian III's quote is the preface of the 1537 Ordinatio, which speaks in the king's voice; the quote is raw OCR with long-s and r-rotunda, as the file holds it. Paul III's quote is from his bull. Kishka's and Cyril VI's are oaths and professions they signed.

ATTRIBUTION RESTS ON CATALOGUE: Judith Sargent Murray's quote is from the continuation 'by a friend', which the file's catalogue names as hers. Hannah More's quote is from a tract signed 'Z', which the file's creator line gives as More's mark.

TRANSLATIONS: many quotes are in a 17th-20th c. translation (Martyrs Mirror English, Morland, Geddes, Blair and Robertson, Lowndes, Brosset, Calder, Anjou). The work field names the translation where the file does.

OCR TEXT: quotes keep the files' OCR exactly (long-s, broken hyphenation such as 'eter- nal', misreadings such as 'Blagwell' and 'Udonai'). They pass the squash check but read roughly; Kishka, Steenoven, Olivetan, Menezes, Christian III and Gregory V are the roughest.

GREGORY V: the quoted encyclical heads Gedeon's documents of 'Gregory from Smyrna', dated 1797. Gregory V was metropolitan of Smyrna before his first patriarchate (1797). The identification rests on that, not on a name in the document itself.

ABRAHAM OF CRETE: his History of Nadir Shah is in the zakaria_ Brosset volume, on the armenian-christianity-era-8 shelf (author slug abraham-of-crete). armenian-apostolic-church-era-8 has no corpus-map shelf, so he is backed by source quote, not held.
MITROFAN: held row is the Life of Paisius 'compiled at Neamt from Mitrofan's account', so it is his account in another's compilation.

YEARS: many years rest on general reference (a first office or first dated work), not on a vendored file or the voices line; each decision's reason names the basis. Person-entry sort years are estimates: martin-luther 1517, john-calvin 1536, william-tyndale 1525, ignatius-of-loyola 1540, john-wesley 1738. If the person entries' own start years differ, the rows must be re-sorted.
WILLIAM TYNDALE: planned person entry placed in the-english-reformation-and-elizabethan-settleme row, though no voices line there names him.

NIKODEMOS IN TWO ROWS: Nikodemos the Hagiorite is a held voice in orthodoxy-under-the-ottomans-parish-millet-and-n (1453-1650) and in the-hesychast-revival-paisius-and-the-philokalia; his dates (1782-1809) fall far after the first entry's span. George Whitefield, Richard Baxter, Patriarch Nikon and Charles Borromeo also appear in two rows each.
